rounds.headline: InlineRename destroyed authored text; the tool dock could not draw its own screenshot; the floating pill split keyboard focus in two.
rounds.mine: The custom colour well was decoration — ControlStrip never forwarded the slot.

rounds.headline: FramesPanel's view menu CRASHED — Base UI's GroupLabel outside a Group — and had shipped that way because no story ever opened it.
rounds.mine: My round-1 toolbar fix regressed the portal case: React context crosses portals, the DOM does not.

rounds.headline: Round 2's answer to a data-loss bug was a comment. The person losing the data never reads the source.
rounds.mine: I broke the registry: the ToolbarBoundary import gave four items a ./toolbar dependency without shipping toolbar.tsx. My own --check said STALE and I had not run it.

rounds.headline: Overlay never overlaid — the port carried the donor's opacity rule and dropped its layout rule.
rounds.mine: The published payloads were serving pre-fix bytes: eight items, including the version that silently ate line breaks.

rounds.headline: Something WAS worse than base: a host calling createPortal got a broken strip. I deleted the mechanism rather than patch it a third time.
rounds.mine: The property it bought never existed — a raw range input cannot join a Base UI composite.

rounds.headline: Base/HEAD fixtures came back identical. The regression was genuinely gone.
rounds.mine: Three assertions were weaker than their own prose; writing the strong one showed my expected order was wrong and the code right.

rounds.headline: A mutation sweep of all 254 play functions found five tests that could not fail — most in stories I never touched.
rounds.mine: My capture script exited 0 after capturing nothing, leaving stale PNGs as apparent evidence.

rounds.headline: The drag handle was aria-hidden AND focusable, and no KeyboardSensor was registered at all.
rounds.mine: process.env.NODE_ENV in copied source broke a DOM-only host where base worked.

rounds.headline: My checker was a re-derivation of a format I do not own. It now delegates to shadcn's own registryItemSchema.
rounds.mine: Object.hasOwn is ES2022 — the second time the kit inherited its own build assumptions into source we hand to strangers.

rounds.headline: No regression against base across 34 items and 89 copied files. A completed keyboard reorder DOES work.
rounds.mine: Two more assertions passed with the behaviour broken; registry metadata drift went unchecked.
